finding: Vikings Warship: the stat panel (nd74LibluQ0 s_03062 51:02 and s_03118 51:58) shows one weapon, '45 Cannonx6 (Siege) +70 vs Building, 9.00 Tiles Range, 5.62s Attack Speed', and the bottom panel reads 45. The gap list has damage 35, which matches the datamine's second (ranged) weapon. The datamine has two weapons: 45 true damage and 35 ranged. The 35 never appears on screen, so the damage field should be rechecked. The panel also shows 1.44 Tiles/s movement against the known 1.25. The player had used cheats ('unc used Cheats!' in chat), likely only for resources.

Dhùn Èideann: the seven Sisters deal Ranged damage, not Siege. Unupgraded values (qlogYcWhKEU s_01820) are 70/70/40/40/30/30/20 damage, with ship bonuses equal to the base (+70/+70/+40/+40/+30/+30/+20 vs Ship). Ranges are 10/10/8.75/8.75/8.75/8/8 tiles and reloads 4.62/4.62/5.62/5.62/6.62/6.62/6.62 s. Two later games (c_oaynL66jY s_01663, wzT5WTqIIU4 s_00648) show every Sister at +2 with the bottom panel reading '70 +2', which is an upgrade, so 70 is the base. The armor panel shows 50 vs Ranged and 0 vs Melee.

'Seven Sisters' cannons are not a separate tech. The landmark tooltip (qlogYcWhKEU s_01754, also in the build menu at c_oaynL66jY 37:45, wzT5WTqIIU4 10:26 and qlogYcWhKEU 7:46) says the landmark is 'Equipped with' them. The finished landmark's command card (s_01820) has only two production buttons and a rally flag. No 'SEVEN SISTERS' research tooltip appears in any OCR'd frame; the only all-caps 'SEVEN SISTERS' text is a video overlay, 'SEVEN SISTERS · SIEGE 100 GOLD CHEAPER', at wzT5WTqIIU4 10:22.

Scots Man-at-Arms: a Feudal MAA before Lochaber Axes was researched (c_oaynL66jY s_00618, 10:18, 120 HP) already shows a third weapon, '10 Lochaber Axe (Melee) +4 vs Cavalry +4 vs Elephants 1.04 Tiles Range 1.12s'. That looks like the brace weapon being displayed early. After the research (s_01431), the main weapon becomes '17 Lochaber Axe (Melee)' (12 +5) with the same +4/+4. An Elite-era panel (c_oaynL66jY 30:14, OCR only) reads '26/22 Lochaber Axe' with +5 vs Cavalry/+5 vs Elephants, so the bonus grows with unit tier. +4/+4 is the standard-tier value.

Bonus damage does not change with blacksmith upgrades in these panels. The Skâne Crossbowman reads +10 vs Heavy at both 9+1 and 9+2. The Highland Archer reads +6 at both 6 and 6+1, and the Scots Crossbowman +10 at both 11 and 11+2. The OCR has an Elite Highland Archer (c_oaynL66jY 30:35-30:58) at +9 vs Light Melee Infantry / +9 vs Light Gunpowder, but I did not open that frame.

Upgrade to Veteran Cateran: the 2-3 s sampling missed this tooltip. In xjYytU_zXTA the player sweeps the Barracks second row at 08:08-08:10. Frames extracted from the mp4 at 0.3 s steps show the D button as 'UPGRADE TO VETERAN, Unit Technology 1/2, 50 food 125 gold 30s, Upgrade Cateran to Veteran Cateran., Requirements: Castle Age (III)'; the full frame was saved as C:/Users/Sam/projects/aoe4-build-crafter/.cache/upcoming-frames/xjYytU_zXTA/x_00489_7.jpg. The F button at 490.7 s is the Elite Gallowglass upgrade. Barracks row 2 reads A Pikemen to Hardened, S Men-at-Arms, D Cateran, F Gallowglass.

Upgrade to Elite Cateran is the one building value without a tooltip on screen. It is inferred as Barracks from the shared D-button chain (Unit Technology 1/2 then 2/2) and from c_oaynL66jY 29:08-29:19. There, 10 selected Barracks research all four row-2 unit upgrades in Imperial Age and four 'Upgrade to Elite completed' notices follow.

Muster Tacksmen appears on two command cards: the Mustering Hall (xjYytU_zXTA 24:48, wzT5WTqIIU4 11:16) and the Three Loch Lookout landmark (qlogYcWhKEU 12:50). Mustering Hall is reported as the base value and Three Loch Lookout as a variant. All four muster tooltips say the warriors are recruited 'to the Mustering Hall'. Muster Tacksmen carries the class line 'Royal Summon', unlike the Highland musters, which say 'Call upon the Highlands'.

Mustering cap: no on-screen maximum exists. The value 4 per Mustering Hall is 1 default charge plus one per Influence tier (Tier 1/2/3 at 3/6/10 structures, qlogYcWhKEU 11:30). The hall's charge counter in the stat panel matches: 1, then 0 after a muster, then 1, 2, 3 as tiers are reached (c_oaynL66jY 17:25-20:35). The Three Loch Lookout adds 3 more, so 4 is a per-hall figure, not a hard cap. Muster costs fall 20% per tier at Tiers 2 and 3: Gallowglass 1350 to 1080 to 810.

Siege Tower building: Scots have no producing building for it. The Siege Engineering tooltip at the Blacksmith says 'Melee and ranged infantry can construct Siege Towers and Battering Rams in the field.', and the Scots Siege Workshop card in Imperial Age (c_oaynL66jY 31:13) has no tower button. This matches the base-game data in units_all.json, where siege towers are produced by infantry units only.

Regional tech discount and Lowland Landmark Technology Discount overlap. I used the civ-overview sentence for the generic regional rule and the Stone of Destiny landmark-slot tooltip for the Lowland one ('Lowland technology costs are reduced by 50%.'). The second-landmark texts say 'further reduced by 50%', for both Lowland and Highland.

Vikings start with 0 food (not the standard 200), plus 200 wood, 100 gold and 0 stone. Two independent recordings show it: Corvinus at 00:01-00:02 (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_00141.jpg and s_00142.jpg) and Drongo at 00:07 (uNw-K34ZDPs/s_00048.jpg). Food is still 0 at 00:35 while villagers went 6/10 to 7/10 (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_00174.jpg), which confirms that Northern Migration villagers cost nothing. That conflicts with the jeando villager record (50 food) and with the BV1dSny6uE4j_p1 villager tooltip that still lists 50 food.

Do not use Beasty's lobby games or the LaSh/xjYytU/BV1Lvn46dEbY sandbox games for starting resources. Beasty (nd74LibluQ0, c_oaynL66jY, BV182n46EEDi_*) had 50000/50050/25000/10000; the others had 100000 of each. Their unit counts (6/10, 1/9, 7/10) still match the standard games.

Vikings Villager Capacity starts at 10 and each Longhouse adds +10 Villager Capacity and +25 max population. The pop cap goes 10 -> 35 -> 60 ... up to 200 (nd74LibluQ0 HUD timeline 6/10 -> 10/20 (11/35) -> 16/30 (17/60)). The highest Villager Capacity in any recording is 200 (nd74LibluQ0 41:40, BV1Bmnx6ZEBh_p2 6:31, BV1Yfnx6nEZM_p1 22:10/48:38). Beasty guessed it is uncapped (transcript 14:54). So 200 may be a hard maximum, but nothing on screen states one.

Folkekirken age conflict (another group's item): Kongens Dør Cathedral is labelled 'Age IV - Economic Landmark' and 'Has a unique technology that further increases maximum population' (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_01500.jpg). The same game shows 128/220 with 'Folkekirken completed' at game 23:13 (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_01532.jpg). Folkekirken is therefore researched at an Imperial landmark, which supports 'Imperial' over the datamined 'Castle'.

Rikets Nyckel Castle alone raises the cap to 210 (BV182n46EEDi_p2/s_00667.jpg: 31/210 right after 'A new age begins'). So '210 regardless of landmark' holds, and 220 needs Kongens Dør plus Folkekirken.

Scots HUD: the '1/9' counter (cow icon) is Highland Cattle count over cattle capacity. The Overview gives starting capacity 9, +4 per Highland Landmark, and 30 food per minute while grazing (BV1Bmnx6ZEBh_p2/s_01200.jpg). The idle counter reads 7 while population reads 7/10, so the starting cattle does not count toward population (inferred from 6 villagers + scout = 7). The second Scots HUD counter, '0/1' with a clock icon, is not explained in any frame I opened.

The Vikings Overview gives Falkr's Village Saga as 'Upgrade 6 Longhouses with attachments' with reward 'Villager recruitment speed reduced by 2 seconds and Longhouse attachment cost reduced by 20%' (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_00012.jpg). That is relevant to the 22 s Northern Migration interval.

Sacred Grove tooltip (BV1djnt6oETG_p1/s_02597.jpg): establish time 10s, '1/3' limit, '+1' armor to nearby units, health regen 5/s if no enemies for 30 s, can capture Sacred Sites. No Berserker spawn interval appears anywhere, so it is listed in notFound.

finding: Folkekirken: Imperial. Its only tooltip (nd74LibluQ0 40:38; same in ehO1BOe7wG8 25:24 and uNw-K34ZDPs 20:20) is in the panel of KONGENS DØR CATHEDRAL, 'Age IV - Economic Landmark', and never shows a Requirements line. The datamined Castle (age 3) value is an internal requirement that can never be met before Imperial.

Snowdoun Gate: neither 52 nor 58 is a base batch time. Both are Highland Archer toggle times with production-speed bonuses. Each toggle has its own cycle; datamined Pikeman 80, Highland Archer 76, Cateran 85, Early MAA 104. A batch is 3 units (the streamer says 'it's always three'; qlogYcWhKEU population 7 to 10). The tooltip counts down while a toggle is ON and is static while OFF. c_oaynL66jY (HA OFF) = 52 s, about 76/1.45. wzT5WTqIIU4 = 58 s at the moment of toggling and 57 s a second later, about 76/1.3; its MAA reads 1m20s and Cateran 1m5s, also base/1.3. The bonus-free run is qlogYcWhKEU at game 01:00-02:17 (Pikeman 1m17s counting down, about 80 s). Which Mustering Hall techs give the +30% and +45% was not verified on screen.

Adjustable Crossbars (Scots): 90 s with no discount. The 59 s at qlogYcWhKEU 12:24 is the time left on a research already a third done (greyed button, progress bar about 1/3), and the completion banner appears 60 s later at game 02:13.

Vikings Villager: 22 s. The tooltip clock is the Northern Migration auto-recruit countdown, not a static time. nd74LibluQ0 goes 01s then 22s the second a villager pops (7/10 to 8/10 at game 00:43-00:44). The Corvinus '20s' (ehO1BOe7wG8 2:46, game 00:27) goes to 18s at 00:29, so it is mid-countdown. Falkr's Village Saga reward ('Villager recruitment speed reduced by 2 seconds') would give 20 s; no frame shows the post-saga reset. Aside for the cost.food gap (not this group): the Vikings villager tooltip in nd74LibluQ0 s_00125 and ehO1BOe7wG8 s_00166 shows only the clock and no food cost.
Bondi: both values are right for different buildings. Barracks 17 s, Longhouse 23 s ('Produces Bondi spearmen but 25% slower'). They are static readings repeated across six videos.

Danevirke wall and Danevirke Gate: Castle. The Danevirke tech says 'Requirements: Castle Age (III)' (researched at the Capital TC for 500 stone, 45s), or Valdemar Castle (Age III landmark) grants it. All wall and gate selections are in Age III or later. The datamined age 1 on the wall and gate records only reflects that they replace palisades.

Dreki Stave Church: Imperial, from its place in the 'IV R' build-menu column (uNw-K34ZDPs s_01440). No tooltip naming it with a Requirements line exists in the footage. Guardian of Scotland: Imperial, from the hovered icon in the 'IV R' column (xjYytU_zXTA s_02438/s_02440).

Vegetable Farm: Dark Age. It is selected while the player is Age I, right after 'Farmstead completed' (nd74LibluQ0 06:41). Side note for its cost and build-time gaps (not this group): the fields come from the Farmstead attachment, whose tooltip reads 200 wood and '02s' (static in the Tech Tree view, BV1Bmnx6ZEBh_p1 s_03152).

Northern Migration cap: starting Villager Capacity is 10 (HUD 6/10 at game 00:10), plus 10 per Longhouse (15/20 with one Longhouse). The highest capacity seen is 200 in three games; no frame shows a hard cap.

Heavy Tunics: Pasture and Loom finished at game 12:56 (vKPxGYSbN2Q s_00741), the countdown reads 268 at 12:58 (s_00743), and 'Sarrock abgeschlossen' comes at about game 17:26. Forge Welding: 'Waffenschmied abgeschlossen' at 13:12 (s_00757), countdown 268 at 13:14 (s_00759) and 266 at 13:16 (s_00760), completion between 17:40 and 17:44. The 262 readings in nd74LibluQ0 were taken a few seconds after the start. Pruned English OCR from BV1Bmnx6ZEBh_p1 agrees: 'RESEARCHING FORGE WELDING 239' at 13:28, 'Forge Welding completed' at 17:27.

Dissent on existing Heavy Tunics building ('Longhouse (Smithy attachment)', marked confirmed): it should be Longhouse (Pasture and Loom). In vKPxGYSbN2Q, Heavy Tunics ('Sarrock', an armor tech) starts in the Longhouse the moment 'Weide und Webstuhl abgeschlossen' appears (s_00741/s_00743). nd74LibluQ0 s_01774 shows the HEAVY TUNICS tooltip in a Longhouse whose panel has the loom attachment icon. Bone Ash Steel runs in the anvil (Smithy) Longhouse (s_01826) and Mail Shirts in the loom Longhouse (s_01812).

All six attachment techs run on one pattern: each starts on its own the moment its attachment exists or a new age begins, and takes 270 s. Tier 1 starts in Age II, tier 2 at the Age III start (26:38), tier 3 at the Age IV start (33:10). The completions match start + 270 within 1-2 s of notification lag. That is the basis for the inferred ages (Feudal/Castle/Imperial) and the inferred 270 s for the tier 2 and 3 techs. No resource drop appears at any research start, which is the evidence for cost n/a.

vKPxGYSbN2Q uses cheats ('LaSh hat Cheats verwendet!', 99k resources). Attachments and the Age III landmark complete instantly; for example, the Smithy is paid and done between 13:10 and 13:12. Research countdowns still tick 1:1 with the in-game clock, so the research times are not affected. Do not use this video for attachment build times.

German-to-English names used: Pressschweißen = Forge Welding, Beinaschenstahl = Bone Ash Steel, Gussstahl = Crucible Steel, Sarrock = Heavy Tunics, Kettenhemden = Mail Shirts, Lamellenpanzer = Lamellar Plating, Waffenschmied = Smithy, Weide und Webstuhl = Pasture and Loom, Gehöft = Farmstead, Bienenkörbe = Bee Skeps. The tier and effect lines confirm the mapping ('Erhöht den Schaden aller Infanterie- und Kavallerieeinheiten' vs 'Erhöht die Fern- und Nahkampfrüstung aller Einheiten außer Belagerungseinheiten').

Attachments (Farmstead, Bee Skeps, Pasture and Loom, Smithy) are not in the gap list; the checklist already has them confirmed, and these frames agree. Smithy and Pasture and Loom show 100 wood, 100 gold, 20 秒 (BV1dSny6uE4j_p1 s_00085). Farmstead shows 200 wood, 02s (BV182n46EEDi_p1 s_01673; BV1dSny6uE4j_p1 s_00069). Bee Skeps shows 200 wood, 20 秒 (BV1dSny6uE4j_p1 s_00073) and 'Generates 50 Gold per minute. Increases Longhouse health by 500.' (BV182n46EEDi_p1 s_01612). BV182n46EEDi_p1 s_03236/s_03206 at 31:39-32:10 show SMITHY and PASTURE AND LOOM at 80 wood / 80 gold. That is the 20% saga discount on Longhouse attachments (Chinese OCR '长屋附件成本降低'), not the base cost.

Bee Skeps actually pay 8 gold every ~10 s (about 48/min), against the tooltip's '50 Gold per minute'. The existing variant value 8 for Bee Skep Production came from the Longhouse panel's '8/min'; 8 is gold per tick, not per minute.
